# Opening: Jesus had no biological father

**Position.** On the KJV text, the child Jesus had a mother, Mary, and no human biological father. Joseph was her husband and the child's legal and caring guardian, but not his begetter. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost."

## 1. The conception is stated as a conception without a man

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** The Greek is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου), "out of the Holy Spirit." *Ek* (G1537) marks source or origin. The source of the conception is named, and it is not Joseph. *Synelthein* (συνελθεῖν, G4905, "to come together") is the word for the couple's coming together, and the text puts the pregnancy *before* it.
**[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The Greek *gennēthen* (γεννηθέν, "begotten, conceived") is joined to *ek pneumatos*. The same verb that elsewhere names a father's act is here assigned to the Holy Ghost.
**[L4]** From the *ek* of source in Matthew 1:18 and the repeated *gennēthen ek pneumatos* in Matthew 1:20, the conceiving is assigned to the Holy Ghost and to no man. The text names only Mary and the Holy Ghost as the two terms of the conception.

## 2. Mary's own question and the answer she was given

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (γινώσκω, G1097) is "to know," used here of sexual knowledge. It is present tense: she is presently knowing no man. *Parthenos* (παρθένος, G3933) in Luke 1:27 means "virgin," and Mary is called "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph."
**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." *Episkiazō* (ἐπισκιάζω, G1982) means "to overshadow." It is not the word of marital union. "Therefore" (*dio*, διό) makes the divine conception the ground of the title "Son of God."
**[L4]** Mary's question, which asks how conception can occur when she knows no man, is answered by naming the Holy Ghost's coming and not any man's. The answer excludes a human begetter because the answer supplies a different cause for the birth.

## 3. Joseph's conduct shows that he was not the father

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
**[L2]** *Apolysai* (ἀπολῦσαι, G630) is "to dismiss, to put away." Joseph was minded to dismiss a wife already found with child, so he knew the child was not his.
**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." *Ginōskō* (G1097) is imperfect (*eginōsken*): he was not knowing her, and "till" (*heōs*, G2193) runs to the birth.
**[L4]** Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph acting as a man who knew he was not the father. Matthew 1:25 shows that he had no relations with Mary through the time of the birth. Together these two verses close off Joseph as biological father.

## 4. The genealogy breaks its own pattern at Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
**[L2]** The verb *egennēsen* (ἐγέννησεν, G1080, "begat") runs through Matthew 1:2-15 as "A begat B." At the last step the verb changes to the passive *egennēthē* (ἐγεννήθη, "was born"). The relative pronoun *hēs* (ἧς, "of whom") is feminine singular, so it refers to Mary and not to Joseph. Joseph is called *ton andra Marias* (τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας, "the husband of Mary").
**[L3]** Matthew 1:20 calls Joseph "thou son of David" and Matthew 1:25 says he "called his name JESUS." Joseph's role is given as taking Mary and naming the child, not begetting him. Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." *Enomizeto* (ἐνομίζετο, G3543) means "was thought, was supposed," so the Joseph connection is marked as a supposition, not a fact.
**[L4]** The text carries the line to Joseph, switches from active "begat" to passive "was born," and shifts the pronoun to the feminine. This gives Joseph legal standing in the line and Mary the only birth-giving relation.

## 5. Prophecy and the body prepared

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
**[L2]** *Almah* (עַלְמָה, H5959) is a young woman of marriageable age, unmarried. The sign is that she *conceives* (*harah*, הָרָה, "is with child") and *bears*.
**[L3]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." Matthew uses *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin") for the same prophecy. Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." The phrase is *genomenon ek gynaikos* (γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός, "come to be out of a woman"). Only the woman is named as source.
**[L4]** Isaiah 7:14 as Matthew 1:23 applies it, together with Galatians 4:4, presents the birth as from a woman and a prophetic virgin with no human father named. This matches the "seed of the woman" language of Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed" (*zera*, זֶרַע, H2233, "seed").

## 6. Jesus' own speech

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
**[L3]** Luke 2:49: "How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Mary says "thy father" of Joseph, and the child answers by pointing to "my Father" in the temple. Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him."
**[L2]** In Luke 2:49 *Patros* (πατρός, G3962) is "father" and the possessive is "my." The child redirects the title from the household to God.
**[L4]** Luke 2:48 uses "thy father" in the sense of the household's recognised father, and Luke 2:49 corrects the direction of the title. Together these show the title in Luke 2:48 is the ordinary one for a guardian. This sense is the one Luke 3:23 qualifies with "as was supposed."

## Anticipated objections

- John 6:42, "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" is what the crowd said. It reports the people's understanding, which is the "supposed" of Luke 3:23.
- Romans 1:3, "made of the seed of David according to the flesh," names David's descent and does not name Joseph as begetter. Matthew 1:20 calls Joseph "son of David," and Luke 1:32 says the Lord God "shall give unto him the throne of his father David," which speaks of the throne.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. The conception is stated to be "of the Holy Ghost" with a named source and no human agent. Footing: Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 [L1], *ek pneumatos hagiou* and *gennēthen* [L2], *synelthein* "before they came together" [L3].
2. Mary was a virgin who knew no man, and the angel's answer supplies a divine cause. Footing: Luke 1:34 [L1], *ginōskō* and *parthenos* [L2], Luke 1:35 "overshadow" and "therefore" [L3].
3. Joseph knew the child was not his, and he did not know Mary until the birth. Footing: Matthew 1:19 [L1], *apolysai* [L2], Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till" [L3].
4. The genealogy shifts from "begat" to "was born" with a feminine "of whom," and Luke 3:23 calls the connection "supposed." Footing: Matthew 1:16 [L1], *egennēsen / egennēthē / hēs* [L2], Luke 3:23 *enomizeto* [L3].
5. Scripture traces the birth to a woman, a virgin, and her seed. Footing: Isaiah 7:14 [L1], *almah* [L2], Galatians 4:4 and Matthew 1:23 [L3].
6. Jesus had no human biological father; he was conceived by the Holy Ghost in Mary, and Joseph was her husband and his guardian, not his begetter. Footing: links 1-5 [L4] resting on Matthew 1:18, 1:20, Luke 1:34-35, Matthew 1:25 [L1/L3] and *ek*, *ginōskō*, *egennēthē* [L2].

# Challenge: the seed is David's according to the flesh, and the named father is Joseph

The defender's keystone, **D6**, says "Jesus had no human biological father." I answer from the rows. The promise names a seed that comes out of a man's body. The text names one man as father: Joseph, of the house of David. Each of the defender's links D1 to D5 reads a verse past what it says.

## My declared chain

**C1. The promised seed comes out of a man's body.**
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12 says: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." The seed comes from David's own body.
- [L3] Acts 2:30 says: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- [L3] Romans 1:3 says: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- [L2] *Osphys* (G3751) means "loins." It is the word in Acts 2:30. It is also the word of Hebrews 7:10, "he was yet in the loins of his father," where a man's descendants are counted in a father. *Sperma* (G4690, "seed") in Romans 1:3 carries *kata sarka*, "according to the flesh."
- [L4] The loins-word and the seed-word, both marked "according to the flesh," require a flesh seed out of David's line through a man's loins.

**C2. Descent is counted by the father's house, and the text names the father.**
- [L1] Hebrews 7:14 says: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L3] Numbers 1:18 says the tribes "declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." Ezra 2:59 shows the other side: those who "could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they were of Israel," were left out.
- [L3] The man of that house is named. Luke 2:4 says Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David." The angel says in Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David." Mary herself says in Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." The disciple says in John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph."
- [L3] Mary's kin is given as Elisabeth, "thy cousin Elisabeth" (Luke 1:36), and Elisabeth "was of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5).
- [L4] Descent that is "evident," counted by the father's house, is made evident through the man the rows name, Joseph of David's house. It is not made evident through Mary, whose stated kin is of Aaron.

**C3. Knowing is the canon's stated means of begetting, and Joseph and Mary were husband and wife.**
- [L1] Genesis 4:1 says: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- [L3] They were husband and wife from the espousal. Matthew 1:19 calls him "Joseph her husband." Matthew 1:20 says "Mary thy wife." Deuteronomy 22:24 calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife."
- [L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is the same verb in Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:25.
- [L4] Joseph, of David's house, knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins. This rests on C1's seed, C2's named father, Genesis 4:1's means, and the husband-and-wife rows.

## Against the defender's links

**D1 ("no human agent")**
- [L1] Matthew 1:20 says: "that which is conceived [Gr. begotten] in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L3] John 1:13 says of believers: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." 1 John 5:1 says: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God."
- [L2] These rows join the same verb, *gennaō* ("beget"), to the same *ek* ("out of"), with God as the source. They are said of men who had human fathers.
- [L4] So "begotten ... of" God is covenant origin, and it stands beside a human father. Romans 1:3 adds *kata sarka* ("according to the flesh") when flesh descent is meant. Matthew 1:20 does not add it.
- [L3] The angel's "for" (*gar*, "for, because") gives the reason for the command "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." The child is the seed God claims: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14).

**D2 (Mary "knew no man," so the answer excludes a begetter)**
- [L1] Luke 1:34 says: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *Ginōskō* here is present tense. It states her condition when the angel spoke.
- [L3] The angel's verbs show presence and power, not begetting. *Eperchomai* ("come upon") is the verb of Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses." *Episkiazō* ("overshadow"; G1982: 5 verses) is the cloud of Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them," and Peter's shadow in Acts 5:15.
- [L3] The title "Son" already stands with the throne before her question. Luke 1:32 says: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The same pairing appears in 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him to be my son." Solomon had a father, David.

**D3 ("he knew the child was not his")**
- [L1] Matthew 1:19 says he was "minded to put her away privily."
- [L2] *Eboulēthē* means "was minded," a word of intent. Its stated grounds are "being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example." It contains no verb of knowing.
- [L3] Matthew 1:25 says "knew her not till she had brought forth." *Heōs* ("till") marks the span up to the birth, and it comes after "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24). Deuteronomy 20:7 names that taking as its own step: "betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
- [L4] So Matthew 1:18's "before they came together" dates the finding before the taking into his house. Matthew 1:25 covers the pregnancy after the taking. Both fit C3.

**D4 (the passive verb and "supposed")**
- [L1] Matthew 1:16 says: "Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
- [L2] *Egennēthē ex hēs* means "was born of her." It names the mother of the birth and does not narrate the begetting.
- [L3] Luke uses *enomizeto* in Luke 3:23. It is the verb form of Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made." Luke 3:23 stands with Luke's own narration: "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27) and "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41).

**D5 ("woman ... her seed")**
- [L1] Galatians 4:4 says "made of a woman."
- [L3] Matthew 11:11 says: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." John's father is named: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son" (Luke 1:13).
- [L3] "Her seed" (Genesis 3:15) has the same form as Hagar's "thy seed" (Genesis 16:10). Hagar's son was Abraham's.
- [L2] Isaiah 7:14 uses *almah* (H5959, "young woman"; 7 verses). Its sign is bounded in Ahaz's day by Isaiah 7:16 and Isaiah 8:3-4. There, "I went unto [Heb. approached] the prophetess; and she conceived."

## UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES

1. **LINK D1:** "the conceiving is assigned to the Holy Ghost and to no man."
   - PRESSED WITH: John 1:13; 1 John 5:1; Romans 1:3. *Gennaō ek* God is said of men who had fathers, and only Romans 1:3 carries "according to the flesh."
2. **LINK D2:** "The answer excludes a human begetter because the answer supplies a different cause."
   - PRESSED WITH: Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34; 1 Chronicles 28:6. These are the angel's verbs of power and presence, and a "my son" title that stands beside a named father.
3. **LINK D3:** "so he knew the child was not his."
   - PRESSED WITH: Matthew 1:19 (*eboulēthē*, intent, with its two stated grounds); Matthew 1:24; Deuteronomy 20:7.
4. **LINK D5:** "Only the woman is named as source."
   - PRESSED WITH: Matthew 11:11 with Luke 1:13; Genesis 16:10.
5. **LINK D6:** "Jesus had no human biological father."
   - PRESSED WITH: 2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30; Hebrews 7:14 with Numbers 1:18; Luke 2:48.
   - The defender must show how a seed "out of thy bowels," "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh," is "evident" by the father's house while the father whom Mary names is set aside.

# Round 2: Jesus had no human biological father

The challenger's chain rests on one move: wherever the text says "seed of David," "loins," or "father," it must mean Joseph's body. I take C1 to C3 first, then the five pressed premises.

## A. Answer to C1: the seed "according to the flesh"

**[L1]** Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
**[L2]** *Osphys* (G3751, "loins") names descent in general. The challenger's own witness shows this. **[L1]** Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." Levi was in Abraham's loins several generations back, so "loins" does not require the immediate father's body. *Sarx* (G4561, "flesh") is glossed on the sheet as "the body ... or as the means of kindred." The flesh of kindred is the body, and Mary supplies a body.
**[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." *Genomenon ek gynaikos* (G1096, "come to be," with "out of a woman") says that Jesus' flesh came out of her. Romans 1:3 says "made of the seed of David according to the flesh," and the "made" is the same *ginomai* verb of Galatians 4:4.
**[L4]** Acts 2:30, Hebrews 7:10 and Galatians 4:4 make "fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" mean David's body-line reaching Jesus through the woman he was "made of." Flesh descent from David is therefore met by Mary. It does not need Joseph's begetting.

**[L1]** Luke 1:32, said to Mary before the conception: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
**[L2]** *Patros* (G3962, "father") is used here of David, many generations back. In the same message that announces the conception, "father" is lineal, not immediate.
**[L4]** So "thy father" in Luke 2:48, which the challenger presses, does not have to mean begetter. The word's range includes ancestor and household head.

**[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
**[L3]** Verse 14 gives the sonship in covenant terms: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son." The same promise reaches Solomon in 1 Chronicles 28:6: "I have chosen him [to be] my son."
**[L2]** *Bachar* (H977, "choose") is election. Luke 1:35 differs: **[L1]** "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." *Dio* (διό, "wherefore") grounds the title in the cause just named, the Holy Ghost coming on her. For Solomon the title rests on God's choice. For the child in Luke 1:35 it rests on the conception.
**[L4]** The Solomon parallel therefore fails on its own wording. Solomon is "chosen," while Jesus is "therefore ... called the Son of God" because of how he is conceived.

## B. Answer to C2: "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda"

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." The verse names the tribe, not the begetter.
**[L3]** Ezra 2:61 gives the precedent for counting through a wife's line: "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name." Matthew 1:21 gives Joseph's act: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25 says "he called his name JESUS."
**[L2]** *Kaleō* (G2564, "to call, name") is the act by which Joseph owns the child into his house and line.
**[L4]** Ezra 2:61 shows the canon recognising a line through a naming legal head, and Matthew 1:21 and 1:25 give Joseph that act. Joseph's place in the register therefore rests on being the legal head and namer.

**[L3]** The challenger's use of Elisabeth is weak. Luke 1:36 gives "thy cousin Elisabeth," and Luke 1:5 says "his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron." A cross-tribe kinship by marriage has precedent in 2 Chronicles 22:11: "the wife of Jehoiada the priest." The text does not state that Mary is not of David. It states only that her kin by marriage is of Aaron.

**[L1]** There is a barrier to Joseph as begetter. Matthew 1:11: "Josias begat Jechonias." Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel." Matthew 1:16 puts Joseph in this line.
**[L3]** Jeremiah 22:30: "for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah."
**[L2]** *Zera* (H2233, "seed") in the Jeremiah verse is the same word the challenger relies on in the promise to David.
**[L4]** Matthew 1:12 and 1:16 place Joseph in Jechonias' line, and Jeremiah 22:30 withholds the throne from his seed. A son begotten by Joseph would be of that seed. The text that carries Joseph in the line also keeps the throne from the seed that line produces, so Joseph is legal head and not begetter.

## C. Answer to C3 and to the D3 press: no window for Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *Synerchomai* (G4905, "to come together") is the couple's union. The pregnancy is found before it.
**[L1]** Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife."
**[L2]** *Paralambanō* (G3880, "receive near, associate with oneself") is the taking into his house.
**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is the verb of Genesis 4:1, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." *Heōs* (G2193, "until") runs to the birth.
**[L4]** The three verses close the timeline. The conception was found before the coming together (1:18). After the taking, he knew her not until the birth (1:25). The challenger proposes that Matthew 1:25 covers only the pregnancy after the taking, with Deuteronomy 20:7 as the separate step. That concedes my point, because by the challenger's own account no moment remains in which Joseph's knowing could have preceded the conception. The challenger's husband-and-wife rows (Matthew 1:19, 1:20, Deuteronomy 22:24) show the legal bond, not the act. Genesis 4:1 makes the act, not the bond, the means, and Matthew 1:25 denies the act through the birth.

**On Joseph's mind:** I rest the weight on the angel's answer. **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *Gar* (G1063, "for") gives the reason. The reason is the source of the conception. If Joseph were the source, there would be nothing for the angel to explain.
**[L3]** Matthew 1:19 shows the case that needed explaining: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man] ... was minded to put her away privily." *Apolyō* (G630, "dismiss, divorce") is what a husband does to a wife found with child by another.
**[L4]** The "fear not ... for" structure of Matthew 1:20 only makes sense if Joseph was not the father.

## D. Pressed premise 1: John 1:13, 1 John 5:1, Romans 1:3

**[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
**[L2]** *Haima* (G129, "blood"), *thelēma* (G2307, "will") and *anēr* (G435, "man") are set against *theos* (G2316, "God"). The verse offers "of man" and "of God" as alternatives, not as co-causes of the one birth. **[L2]** *Gennaō* (G1080) is glossed on the sheet: "figuratively, to regenerate." The believers' birth is a regeneration, and the verse itself says it is "not of blood."
**[L3]** 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God." The believing in this verse marks the birth as spiritual.
**[L4]** John 1:13 and 1 John 5:1 mark their "of God" as figurative by the believing and by the contrast with blood. Matthew 1:20 marks its "of the Holy Ghost" as literal by its object: "that which is conceived in her," which is in the womb. Matthew 1:18 confirms it with "found with child." The same preposition does not carry the same sense when the objects differ. I answer the Romans 1:3 press in section A: the "flesh" is met through the woman.

## E. Pressed premise 2: Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34, 1 Chronicles 28:6

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
**[L2]** *Andra* (G435, "man, husband") is the word for the husband in Matthew 1:16. She is already espoused (Luke 1:27) and expects to be married.
**[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son."
**[L4]** If the angel's promise meant a conception to come through marriage, her question would have an obvious answer. The angel's reply in Luke 1:35 names the Holy Ghost coming upon her and not a husband. Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34 show the verbs *epercomai* (G1904, "come upon") and *episkiazō* (G1982, "overshadow") can describe presence and power. Here they stand as the answer to "How shall this be?" and the cause for the "therefore." That cause is stated. The challenger's alternative has no verse in Luke 1:35.

## F. Pressed premise 3: Matthew 1:19, 1:24, Deuteronomy 20:7

The challenger is right that *boulomai* (G1014, "be minded") is a word of intent, and that Matthew 1:19 has no verb of knowing. I rest D3 instead on section C, which is the chain of Matthew 1:18, 1:20, 1:24 and 1:25. **[L3]** Deuteronomy 20:7 distinguishes "betrothed" from "taken." That distinction is exactly what Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 use to close the timeline.

## G. Pressed premise 4: Matthew 11:11, Genesis 16:10

I concede that "made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4), "born of women" (Matthew 11:11), and "her seed" (Genesis 3:15 beside Genesis 16:10) do not by themselves exclude a father. **[L4]** That sub-claim floats alone. It stands only together with Matthew 1:18-20 and Luke 1:34-35, which name the source. Matthew 11:11 and Luke 1:13 say "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son," with the father addressed. Luke 1:31 says "thou shalt conceive in thy womb," with no father in the promise.

**On Isaiah 7:14.** **[L1]** Isaiah 7:11: "ask it either in the depth, or in the height above." **[L2]** *Oth* (H226, "sign") is a wonder. **[L3]** Isaiah 7:13: "Hear ye now, O house of David." Isaiah 8:3 names the prophetess's son "Mahershalalhashbaz," not Immanuel. **[L4]** The sign of 7:14 is not the birth of 8:3, which has a different name. Matthew 1:22-23 applies the passage to the birth of Jesus with *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin").

## H. Pressed premise 5: the "father whom Mary names"
